title: Coefficient cocycle for normalized open scalar comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and unital maps $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the geometric derived adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and write $T_T^{A,B}=(-)\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ and $\alpha_{T,E}:T_T^{B,C}T_T^{A,B}E\xrightarrow{\sim}T_T^{A,C}E$ for scalar extension and associativity [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion and use the sectionwise sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $e_{j,M}^{A,B}:T_Z^{A,B}j_!^AM\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^BT_U^{A,B}M$ be exactly the normalized isomorphism of [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. For every $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$,
$$e_{j,M}^{A,C}\circ\alpha_{Z,j_!^AM}
=j_!^C(\alpha_{U,M})\circ e_{j,T_U^{A,B}M}^{B,C}\circ T_Z^{B,C}(e_{j,M}^{A,B}).$$
No boundedness, constructibility, coefficient flatness, finite projective dimension, or quasi-compactness of $j$ is required.

source.place: Steps 1 and 4: extension-by-zero scalar maps and their coefficient associativity; first paragraph of returned Step 11

proof.text: Write $S_T^{A,B}=T_T^{A,B}$, let $R_T^{A,B}$ be exact derived restriction of scalars, and put $P_A=j_A^*$ and $J_A=J_j^A$. The scalar adjunction $S_T^{A,B}\dashv R_T^{A,B}$ is the normalized unbounded adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]; $J_A\dashv P_A$ and the coordinate isomorphism $r_A:j_!^A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_A$ are those fixed by [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. Use composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] throughout. Let $\chi^{A,B}:R_U^{A,B}P_B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_AR_Z^{A,B}$ be the inverse-image comparison $b$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], with $u=j$ and constant-ring maps. By the definition of $\beta$, its right-adjoint conjugate is exactly $\chi^{A,B}$; this fixes the direction as well as the map.

source.place: Step 1, normalized open scalar comparison; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint)

proof.text: Transpose the ordinary restriction/pullback squares using their specified pullback/direct-image adjunctions. The resulting direct-image comparisons and restriction-composition comparisons act identically on every section. The mates equivalence, including whiskering at the top and bottom, therefore gives the ordinary coefficient pasting equation. Apply the exact-square composition theorem to descend this equation to the unbounded derived categories, retaining its canonical derived-composition comparisons. Cancel the inverse restriction compositors to obtain the right-adjoint pasting equation used in Step 4.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), identified-coefficient exact inverse images; elementary restriction-action calculation and localization

proof.text: Apply lem-sp-scalar-associator-conjugate at U and Z. It identifies the right conjugate of each inverse prescribed scalar associator with pbcDerivedRestrictComp. This is solely the scalar normalization part of the argument; Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 supply the geometric square coherence and coordinate transport.

Consider the two natural maps from $S_Z^{B,C}S_Z^{A,B}J_A$ to $J_CS_U^{A,C}$. Under the composite adjunctions their right conjugates run from $R_U^{A,C}P_C$ to $P_AR_Z^{A,B}R_Z^{B,C}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3), and the identifications of Steps 1 and 3, the conjugate of $\beta^{A,C}\circ(\alpha_ZJ_A)$ is $(P_A\rho_Z)\circ\chi^{A,C}$, whereas the conjugate of
$$ (J_C\alpha_U)\circ(\beta^{B,C}S_U^{A,B})\circ(S_Z^{B,C}\beta^{A,B}) $$
is $(\chi^{A,B}R_Z^{B,C})\circ(R_U^{A,B}\chi^{B,C})\circ(\rho_UP_C)$. Step 2 equates these. Injectivity of the conjugate correspondence [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives the equality of the two displayed left-adjoint maps. All intermediate objects are in the full unbounded categories; none of the adjunctions imposes a Tor or boundedness condition.

source.place: Step 4, coefficient composition; explicit conjugate calculation using categories.tex Tag 0B65

proof.text:
It remains to express this equality in the prescribed sectionwise coordinates. By [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], at $M$ one has
$$e^{A,B}_M=r_{B,S_U^{A,B}M}^{-1}\circ\beta^{A,B}_M\circ S_Z^{A,B}(r_{A,M}).$$
Expanding the two successive $e$'s, functoriality cancels $S_Z^{B,C}(r_B)$ against $S_Z^{B,C}(r_B^{-1})$. Thus the right side of the desired identity becomes
$$j_!^C(\alpha_{U,M})\circ r_{C,S_U^{B,C}S_U^{A,B}M}^{-1}\circ\beta^{B,C}_{S_U^{A,B}M}\circ S_Z^{B,C}(\beta^{A,B}_M)\circ S_Z^{B,C}S_Z^{A,B}(r_{A,M}).$$
Naturality of $r_C$ moves $j_!^C(\alpha_U)$ through $r_C^{-1}$, replacing the initial pair by $r_{C,S_U^{A,C}M}^{-1}\circ J_C(\alpha_{U,M})$. Step 4 replaces the three middle factors by $\beta^{A,C}_M\circ\alpha_{Z,J_AM}$. Finally naturality of $\alpha_Z$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](4) gives
$$\alpha_{Z,J_AM}\circ S_Z^{B,C}S_Z^{A,B}(r_{A,M})=S_Z^{A,C}(r_{A,M})\circ\alpha_{Z,j_!^AM}.$$
The resulting composite is exactly $e^{A,C}_M\circ\alpha_{Z,j_!^AM}$. This proves the stated identity for the actual normalized $e$, including empty opens, arbitrary unbounded $M$ and nonflat coefficient maps.

lean.statement: theorem proEtaleOpenScalarCocycle (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (hA : ∃ n : ℕ, (ℓ : A) ^ n = 0) (hB : ∃ n : ℕ, (ℓ : B) ^ n = 0) (hC : ∃ n : ℕ, (ℓ : C) ^ n = 0) (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C) {U Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j] (M : proEtaleDerivedCategory U A) : (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Z).hom.app ((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j A).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) ≫ (reductionOpenScalarIso (ψ.comp φ) j).hom.app M = (scalarExtensionFunctor ψ Z).map ((reductionOpenScalarIso φ j).hom.app M) ≫ (reductionOpenScalarIso ψ j).hom.app ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ U).obj M) ≫ (sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j C).mapDerivedCategory.map ((scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ U).hom.app M)
